items.title: Emmanuel Sayles Interview, 1961-01-29
items.q: Lawrence Moray was around, but John Moray was in New York at that time... I believe he died up in New York. Yeah, he died, I heard about him, yeah the person there.

ctx.x: John was the best, yeah. And I had another fellow player with Sidney Desby named Percy Sevier. Well, he wasn't playing so much when he came, but after he had been around, he got to be a very good banjo player too. Then we were like, around in the mid-30s, we had Homer Eugene, we had Randy Hall, and had another fellow named Paul, I can't hear his name, Paul Sufferman, and Sidney Fludger, well, he did a lot of singing, and he also played nice banjo too. I could say, Lawrence Moray was around, but John Moray was in…
you know, yeah. So you were working with that trio for quite a while, I guess.

items.title: Emmanuel Sayles Interview, 1959-01-17
items.q: And in his rhythm section, who was on drums? I know John Moray was still on banjo

ctx.x: He had, they had him so long on that number, Josephine. They were still popping on that number, and he had played that famous saxophone solo on that, see. And in his rhythm section, who was on drums? I know John Moray was still on banjo, and I think Simon was living here, I think Simon was playing bass with him. And who do you have on drums?
Was this after Chani or before?
